title: The mask, target film and stop layer have different jobs
caption: A successful etch transfers geometry through the target while preserving enough mask and underlying material. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Patterned mask
nodes.detail: Protects the regions intended to remain.

nodes.label: Target film
nodes.detail: Exposed regions must be removed to the intended depth.

nodes.label: Etch-stop layer
nodes.detail: The underlying layer should survive the removal step.

nodes.label: Substrate
nodes.detail: The retained structure supports subsequent fabrication.

source.heading: What an Etch Has to Deliver

title: Chemical selectivity and directionality are different properties
caption: Wet chemistry can strongly distinguish materials while also attacking laterally beneath a mask. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Protected top surface
nodes.detail: The mask limits access from above.

nodes.label: Lateral chemical attack
nodes.detail: An isotropic etchant also reaches exposed sidewalls.

nodes.label: Material selectivity
nodes.detail: Different reaction rates can preserve an underlying material.

source.heading: Wet Etch: Still the Workhorse for Selectivity

title: The plasma creates reactive species and directed ions
caption: Electrons sustain the discharge; the sheath near the wafer accelerates ions toward the surface. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Feed gas and electrons
nodes.detail: Electron collisions create ions and reactive fragments.

nodes.label: Plasma bulk
nodes.detail: Charged and neutral reactive species coexist.

nodes.label: Sheath electric field
nodes.detail: The near-surface field accelerates positive ions.

nodes.label: Biased wafer
nodes.detail: Ion arrival helps make removal directional.

title: Ion assistance changes what radicals can remove
caption: Chemical reaction and physical bombardment can reinforce each other; the combined process is not merely their independent sum. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Chemical radicals
nodes.detail: Reactive neutrals form volatile products at exposed material.

nodes.label: Physical ions
nodes.detail: Energetic impact transfers momentum and breaks bonds.

nodes.label: Ion-assisted reaction
nodes.detail: Bombardment enables or accelerates directed surface chemistry.

source.heading: Etch Mechanisms: Chemical, Physical, and the Synergy Between Them

title: Transfer a thin resist image into a tougher mask
caption: A hardmask preserves the pattern during a deeper etch, then is stripped when its job is finished. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Thin resist pattern
nodes.detail: Lithography defines the initial image.

nodes.label: Hardmask transfer
nodes.detail: The image is etched into a more durable film.

nodes.label: Target etch
nodes.detail: The hardmask protects selected regions during removal.

nodes.label: Strip remaining mask
nodes.detail: Remove temporary masking material without harming the device.

title: Different features expose different etch constraints
caption: Isolation trenches, gate structures and deep memory holes ask for different depth, profile and selectivity combinations. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Isolation trench
nodes.detail: Profile and silicon surface quality affect device isolation.

nodes.label: Gate or channel feature
nodes.detail: Tiny dimensions require tight selectivity and damage control.

nodes.label: Deep memory opening
nodes.detail: High aspect ratio makes transport and profile control difficult.

source.heading: The Critical Etches in a Modern Flow

title: Modify one surface layer, then remove it
caption: ALE separates a saturating surface reaction from removal, limiting how much material a cycle can consume. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Surface modification
nodes.detail: Reactant changes the accessible top layer.

nodes.label: Purge
nodes.detail: Remove excess reactant before the next step.

nodes.label: Activated removal
nodes.detail: A controlled step removes the modified material.

nodes.label: Renewed surface
nodes.detail: The exposed surface is ready for another cycle.

source.heading: Atomic Layer Etching and Selective Removal

returnLabel: Repeat the surface-reaction cycle only until the target removal

title: The chamber is part of the process state
caption: Endpoint signals and chamber condition must be interpreted together to keep removal repeatable. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Conditioned chamber
nodes.detail: Walls and consumables establish a starting state.

nodes.label: Run the etch
nodes.detail: The wafer and chamber surfaces change during processing.

nodes.label: Monitor endpoint
nodes.detail: Signals indicate progress toward clearing the film.

nodes.label: Clean and match
nodes.detail: Maintenance restores conditions and aligns chamber behavior.

source.heading: Running an Etch in Production: Endpoint, Chamber Matching, Consumables

title: Several plasma effects can damage a device
caption: Electrical charging, energetic collisions and radiation act through different paths; mitigation must address the relevant mechanism. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Charging imbalance
nodes.detail: Unequal currents can stress connected gate dielectrics.

nodes.label: Ion impact
nodes.detail: Collisions disturb lattice or surface structure.

nodes.label: Plasma radiation
nodes.detail: Photons can alter sensitive materials.

nodes.label: Device reliability
nodes.detail: Unintended changes can reduce yield or lifetime.

title: A cluster tool shares vacuum transport among chambers
caption: Load locks isolate the vacuum hub while a robot routes wafers to qualified process chambers. Schematic, not to scale.

nodes.label: Atmospheric load port
nodes.detail: A carrier supplies wafers to the tool.

nodes.label: Load lock
nodes.detail: The transfer chamber changes pressure without venting the hub.

nodes.label: Vacuum robot
nodes.detail: Central handling selects the next chamber.

nodes.label: Process chamber
nodes.detail: A dedicated module performs the qualified etch recipe.
